when: after an adversarial code review (a separate Sonnet reviewer, CPU only) and before ANY real-model run of E13; the only executions so far are the tiny-model CPU smoke and unit tests (54 passing)
status: design-hardening; no prediction, margin, threshold or decision rule of the prereg is changed

changes.determinism: configure_determinism() at the start of the coordinator and every worker/host: CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8, flash and mem-efficient SDPA disabled (math SDPA), torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True). Reason: the review noted that sm75 SDPA falls to a mem-efficient backward that is not guaranteed deterministic, which could fail the identity control for GPU-numerics reasons. The identity tolerance stays 1e-6 and S1/S1t vs S0 stays the rule.
changes.diagnostic_twin: S0b: the first seed's S0 is run twice in-process; max|diff| between the two final LoRA vectors is stored as identity_noise_floor and printed next to identity_vs_s0. It is a diagnostic: it never changes a control outcome.
changes.memory: S0 records torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved(); before spawning process workers a preflight checks M x (peak + 0.45 GiB) against torch.cuda.mem_get_info() and falls back to thread hosting (recorded as hosting_fallback) or raises the fail-fast if even one host does not fit. Workers run with PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True. Qwen-0.5B with 4 OS processes was estimated at 4-5.5 GB each by the review, i.e. possibly not fitting 14.5 GiB; the fallback makes the cell run (thread-hosted peers share one frozen model) instead of failing, and the hosting actually used is reported per cell. Thread-hosted S1t is the accepted equivalent for the identity control.
changes.evaluation_scheme: the global mixture held-out loss is evaluated at versions 0, 3 and 6 only (the loss_curve keys are '0','3','6'; the S0 gate at round 3 and the final loss at round 6 are the registered quantities), and the evaluation of version v is done by worker (v mod M) when alive, else the lowest alive id. Reason: in the first build worker 0 (the code domain) evaluated every version, delaying its next round and systematically disadvantaging that domain in the K<M cells (a confound for P13b). S0 uses the same versions.
changes.held_out_sampling: the 16 sequences per domain are stride-sampled evenly across the whole held-out region (last 20% of the domain's token stream) instead of the first 16 contiguous sequences, identically for every cell and seed; sha256 and the indices are recorded. Reason: first-16-contiguous tied the metric to a few documents.
changes.hang_protection: startup deadline min(cell_timeout, 900 s); per-round stall watchdog (max(600 s, 20 x median round latency), 1800 s before the first round) and 60 s heartbeat; churn/straggle specs may not target worker 0; --cell-timeout default 3600 s; a worker parent-death watchdog (os._exit when the parent disappears) and an atexit/SIGTERM cleanup so that no worker outlives a killed run; the queue starts each job in its own session and kills the process group at its deadline.
changes.failure_handling: any non-FailFast exception in a cell is recorded as {status: failed, error, traceback_tail} and the invocation continues with the next cell; a model with any failed cell has controls_all_passed False; --resume retries failed cells; the aggregator tolerates failed and missing cells.
changes.fail_fast_additions: (a) after round 1 of the first S0 run the total wall time is projected from the measured seconds per inner step and the number of runs still to do (x1.15); exit 3 if it exceeds --max-hours (default 3.0), for every model including those without a registered step-time assumption; (b) a non-finite round-0 loss aborts (fp16 overflow of a bf16-native model); (c) the learning gate treats NaN as failing; (d) a non-finite evaluation inside a swarm cell marks that cell failed.
changes.granite_experts_implementation: Granite models are loaded with experts_implementation='eager' (override --experts-impl). Reason: the transformers 5.17 default grouped_mm falls back on sm75 to a Python loop with host syncs and computes weight gradients for the frozen experts. The choice only affects speed, not the maths; the value used is recorded.
changes.wire_codec: codeword transport uses int8 and falls back to int16 (tagged) when a codeword exceeds the int8 range, instead of crashing a worker; the number of int16 posts is reported; the byte accounting for P13c counts the bodies actually sent.
changes.ef_semantics: documented, not changed: the error-feedback carry assumes the delta was applied; deltas discarded as late, outside the grace window or from a stale incarnation make the EF guarantee inexact for that worker-round.
changes.bookkeeping: per-model raw files (E13_swarm_local_raw_<model>.json), an existing raw file is archived rather than overwritten, the report merges per-model sections, and the scratch directory is under the OS temp dir.

unchanged: models, domains, workers, cells S0-S5, rounds 6 x 20 inner steps, optimizer and outer settings, P13a-P13d and their rules and thresholds (including the 0.5 retention margin and the 0.30 wire ratio), controls, learning gate 0.05 nats at round 3, qwen0.5b step-time gate (0.585 s/step), data split (first 50% train, last 20% held-out) and the scope limits
queue_plan: three resumable jobs, qwen0.5b (all cells, seeds 1-3), granite1b (S0-S2, seeds 1-3), granite3b (S0-S2, seed 1), run before the remaining exploratory E11b jobs; the E13 queue entries have no output-exists skip, relying on --resume
